parts.title: 第貳部分：非選擇題（占28分）
parts.instructions: 說明：本部分共有二題，請依各題指示作答，答案必須寫在「答案卷」上，並標明大題號（一、二）。作答務必使用筆尖較粗之黑色墨水的筆書寫，且不得使用鉛筆。

sections.title: 一、詞彙題（占15分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1題至第15題，每題有4個選項，其中只有一個是正確或最適當的選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

questions.stem: John’s clock is not functioning _____. The alarm rings even when it’s not set to go off.
Michael has decided to _____ a career in physics and has set his mind on becoming a professor.
Peter plans to hike in a _____ part of Africa, where he might not meet another human being for days.
People in this community tend to _____ with the group they belong to, and often put group interests before personal ones.
I mistook the man for a well-known actor and asked for his autograph; it was really _____.
After spending most of her salary on rent and food, Amelia _____ had any money left for entertainment and other expenses.
In the Bermuda Triangle, a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean, some airplanes and ships were reported to have mysteriously disappeared without a _____.
Shouting greetings and waving a big sign, Tony _____ the passing shoppers to visit his shop and buy the freshly baked bread.
With a continuous 3 km stretch of golden sand, the beach attracts artists around the world each summer to create amazing _____ with its fine soft sand.
The clouds parted and a _____ of light fell on the church, through the windows, and onto the floor.
Instead of a gift, Tim’s grandmother always _____ some money in the birthday card she gave him.
While winning a gold _____ is what every Olympic athlete dreams of, it becomes meaningless if it is achieved by cheating.
The thief went into the apartment building and stole some jewelry. He then _____ himself as a security guard and walked out the front gate.
Due to numerous accidents that occurred while people were playing Pokémon GO, players were advised to be _____ of possible dangers in the environment.
Sherlock Holmes, a detective in a popular fiction series, has impressed readers with his amazing powers of _____ and his knowledge of trivial facts.

sections.title: 二、綜合測驗（占15分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第16題至第30題，每題一個空格，請依文意選出最適當的一個選項，並畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
You begin to notice a bit of pain on your eyelid each time you blink. You [[16]] the mirror to find a tiny red spot on the base of your lower lashes. These [[17]] are probably the beginning of an eye stye.
An eye stye is a small bump, resembling a pimple, that develops when an oil gland at the edge of an eyelid becomes infected by bacteria. These bacteria are found in the nose and are easily [[18]] to the eye when you rub your nose, then your eye. Pus will build up in the center of the stye, causing a yellowish spot. Usually a stye is accompanied by a swollen eye.
[[19]] a stye can look unpleasant at times, it is usually harmless and doesn’t cause vision problems. Most styes heal on their own within a few days. You might speed up healing time by gently pressing a warm washcloth [[20]] your eyelid for 10 minutes, 3 or 4 times a day. Make sure you don’t squeeze or pop a stye like you would a pimple. Doing so may cause a severe eye infection.

groups.passage:
Shoes are hugely important for protecting our feet, especially in places like Africa, where healthcare provision is limited. Unfortunately, shoes are not always readily available for people living in poverty, [[21]] shoes that are the right size. Almost as soon as a child receives shoes to wear, he/she is likely to have grown out of them. Then the child has to [[22]] with shoes that are too small. The Shoe That Grows, created by a charity called Because International, changes all this. It allows children to [[23]] their shoes’ size as their feet grow.
The innovative footwear resembles a common sandal and is made of leather straps and rubber soles, a material similar to that used in tires. They come [[24]] two sizes, and can expand in three places. The straps on the heel and toe control the length of the shoe, [[25]] the two on either side allow for different widths. With this special design, the shoes can “grow” up to five sizes and last for at least five years.

groups.passage:
Research has proven that weather plays a part in our moods: Warmer temperatures and exposure to sunshine increase positive thinking, whereas cold, rainy days bring anxiety and fatigue. [[26]], many people believe that bad weather can reduce productivity and efficiency.
There is, however, a significant [[27]] between such beliefs and the actual effect of weather on people’s performance at work. Using empirical data from laboratory experiments [[28]] observations of a mid-sized Japanese bank in real life, researchers find that weather conditions indeed influence a worker’s focus. When the weather is bad, individuals tend to focus more on their work rather than thinking about activities they could [[29]] outside of work. But photos showing outdoor activities, such as sailing on a sunny day or walking in the woods, can greatly distract workers and thus [[30]] their productivity. The findings conclude that workers are actually most productive when the weather is lousy—and only if nothing reminds them of good weather.

sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31題至第40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
The widespread popularity of onions is not limited to modern-day kitchens. There is evidence of onions being used for culinary and medicinal purposes all over the ancient world. Nonetheless, no culture [[31]] onions quite as much as the ancient Egyptians. For them, the onion was not just food or medicine; it held significant [[32]] meaning. Onions were considered to be [[33]] of eternal life. The circle-within-a-circle structure of an onion, for them, [[34]] the eternity of existence. According to certain documents, ancient Egyptians also used onions for medicinal purposes, but they likely would have viewed the [[35]] power of the vegetable as magical, rather than medical.
Onions are depicted in many paintings [[36]] inside pyramids and tombs that span the history of ancient Egypt. They [[37]] as a funeral offering shown upon the altars of the gods. The dead were buried with onions and onion flowers on or around various [[38]] of their bodies. Mummies have also been found with onions and onion flowers [[39]] their pelvis, chest, ears, eyes, and feet.
Some scholars theorize that onions may have been used for the dead because it was believed that their strong scent would [[40]] the dead to breathe again. Other researchers believe it was because onions were known for their special curative properties, which would be helpful in the afterlife.

sections.title: 四、閱讀測驗（占32分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41題至第56題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得2分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage: Is your dog an Einstein or a Charmer? For US $60, a recently-founded company called Dognition will help you learn more about your dog’s cognitive traits. It offers an online test telling you about the brain behind the bark. Dognition’s test measures a dog’s intellect in several aspects—from empathy to memory to reasoning skills. But don’t expect it to measure your pet’s IQ. Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders, says a dog’s intelligence can’t be described with a single number. Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs. The question is what type your dog relies on more. After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog: For example, how excited does your dog get around other dogs, or children? Do fireworks scare your pup? Then, Dognition guides you through tests that are as fun as playing fetch or hide-and-seek. At the end, you get a report of your dog’s cognitive profile. Your dog could fall into one of nine categories: Ace, Stargazer, Maverick, Charmer, Socialite, Protodog, Einstein, Expert, or Renaissance Dog. That can give you something to brag about on Dognition’s Facebook page. It also can shed new light on why dogs do the things they do. For example, a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes. Dognition helps people understand their dogs in ways that they have never been able to do. This new understanding can enrich the relationship between dogs and their owners.

groups.passage:
Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals. It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head. Although Capoeira appears dancelike, many of its basic techniques are similar to those in other martial arts.
Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves. It is believed that the martial art was connected with tribal fighting in Africa, in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman. In the sixteenth century, when the Africans were taken from their homes to Brazil against their will and kept in slavery, Capoeira began to take form among the community of slaves for self-defense. But it soon became a strong weapon in the life-or-death struggle against their oppressors. When the slave owners realized the power of Capoeira, they began to punish those who practiced it. Capoeiristas learned to camouflage the forbidden fights with singing, clapping, and dancing as though it were simply entertainment.
At first, Capoeira was considered illegal in Brazil. However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style. He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport. He and Mestre Pastinha were the first to open schools, and the Capoeira tree grew, spreading its branches across the world. Nowadays, it is performed in movies and music clips. Capoeira is also believed to have influenced several dancing styles like breaking and hip-hop.

options.B: It was initially created as a type of dance and ritual.
options.C: It was mainly performed to protect a bride or desired woman.
options.D: It was officially recognized in Brazil through the effort of Mestre Bimba.

groups.passage: Winslow Homer (1836-1910) is regarded by many as the greatest American painter of the nineteenth century. Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company. Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books. He then moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance illustrator with Harper’s Weekly, a popular magazine of the time, and began painting. Homer was assigned to cover the inauguration of President Lincoln and, later, the Civil War. His pictures of the Union troops won international recognition. Homer moved to England and, after a two-year stay, returned to America. He settled permanently in Maine in 1883. From the late 1850s until his death in 1910, Winslow Homer produced a body of work distinguished by its thoughtful expression and its independence from artistic conventions. A man of multiple talents, Homer excelled equally in the arts of illustration, oil painting, and watercolor. Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life. Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature. This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art. It shows his extraordinary career from the battlefields, farmland, and coastal villages of America, to the North Sea fishing village of Cullercoats, the rocky coast of Maine, the Adirondacks, and the Caribbean. The exhibition offers viewers an opportunity to experience and appreciate the breadth of his remarkable artistic achievement.

options.D: In an encyclopedia on the art of printing.

groups.passage: Tea, the most typical English drink, became established in Britain because of the influence of a foreign princess, Catherine of Braganza, the queen of Charles II. A lover of tea since her childhood in Portugal, she brought tea-drinking to the English royal court and set a trend for the beverage in the seventeenth century. The fashion soon spread beyond the circle of the nobility to the middle classes, and tea became a popular drink at the London coffee houses where people met to do business and discuss events of the day. Many employers served a cup of tea to their workers in the middle of the morning, thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.” However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people. It came with a high price tag and tea was taxed as well. Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,” a ceremony taking place at about four o’clock. Until then, people did not usually eat or drink anything between lunch and dinner. At approximately the same time, the Earl of Sandwich popularized a new way of eating bread—in thin slices, with something (e.g., jam or cucumbers) between them. Before long, a small meal at the end of the afternoon, involving tea and sandwiches, had become part of the British way of life. As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, its popularity spread right through all corners of the British society. Thus, tea became Britain’s favorite drink. In working-class households, it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor. This meal has become known as “high tea.” Today, tea can be drunk at any time of the day, and accounts for over two-fifths of all beverages consumed in Britain—with the exception of water.

questions.label: 中譯英1
questions.stem: 玉山(Jade Mountain)在冬天常常覆蓋著厚厚的積雪，使整個山頂閃耀如玉。
questions.scoring_notes:
評分標準與歷年相同，在「中譯英」部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。
今年的「中譯英」題目以臺灣景點玉山積雪的風景及其受登山者喜好為主題，內容貼近學生學習經驗，測驗考生是否能以英語描述周遭環境。題目提供主題字「玉山」的英文拼音(Jade Mountain)，第一句讓學生翻譯出「玉山在冬天常常覆蓋著厚厚的積雪，使整個山頂閃耀如玉」。第二句則為「征服玉山一直是國內外登山者最困難的挑戰之一」。使用的字都在詞彙表四級內之詞彙，測驗的重點在於考生能否運用常用的詞彙與基本句型將兩句中文翻譯成正確達意的英文句子，所測驗之句型亦為高中生熟悉的範圍，中等程度以上的考生，如果能使用正確句型並注意用字、拼字，應能得理想的分數。我們發現有不少考生對於英文詞彙的語意及使用，以及英文拼字仍有加強的空間，如第一句的「整個山頂」有許多考生未譯出「整個」 entire 或 whole，「覆蓋著」未用被動語態 is covered；第二句很多學生「征服」不會拼寫或未用動名詞的形式 conquering，也有不少考生「挑戰」的英文 challenges 拼字錯誤，或未用複數(因為是「最困難的挑戰之一」)，相當可惜。

patterns: ..., making + O + V（分詞構句表結果）

figures.label: 四格連環圖片
figures.description: 黑白手繪四格漫畫，排成2×2方格，中央小方格標示閱讀順序「1 2／3 4」（左上1、右上2、左下3、右下4）。圖1（左上）：晴天（左上角畫著太陽）。一家三口準備出遊：戴眼鏡的爸爸哼著歌（頭旁畫有音符），正把一個有提把的袋子（或小箱子）放進休旅車掀起的後車廂，腳邊放著一個行李箱；長捲髮的媽媽和綁著兩條辮子的女兒站在車旁，面帶笑容。圖2（右上）：一家人的車子卡在車陣中，前後左右擠滿了貨車與轎車；駕駛座的爸爸和副駕駛座的媽媽皺著眉頭、一臉不悅，女兒則從後座車窗往外看，面帶微笑。圖3（左下）：抵達目的地——一棟有拱形窗戶與欄杆的大型建築（景點）前，黑壓壓擠滿了人潮（畫了大量人頭）；右下角前景的爸爸（頭上畫著「!!」）、張大嘴巴的媽媽與女兒看到人山人海，露出驚訝、錯愕的表情。圖4（右下）：空白，只畫了一個大問號「?」，由考生想像故事的後續發展與結局。圖中沒有其他文字。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 提示︰請仔細觀察以下三幅連環圖片的內容，並想像第四幅圖片可能的發展，然後寫出一篇涵蓋每張圖片內容且結局完整的故事。
questions.scoring_notes:
「英文作文」的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字四個項目給分，字數明顯不足的作文則扣總分 1 分。
第二大題是「英文作文」，今年為看圖寫作，考生必須根據所提供的三幅連環圖片內容，並想像第四幅圖片可能的發展，寫出一篇涵蓋每張圖片內容且結局完整的故事，文長至少 120 個單詞。
今年作文回到學生熟悉的看圖寫作，以四格漫畫方式引導學生寫出全家出遊遇到塞車，到了目的地也是人山人海的景色。第四格圖片為一個問號，讓學生發揮思考，想像最後圖中人物會做什麼決定或有什麼感想。大部分考生均以全家出遊塞車來描述前兩個圖的情境，第三個圖的場景則較多元，有遊樂園、博物館、動物園、演唱會等休閒場所，也有學生融入時事，以遊行示威人潮或出國過海關等場景為主題，最後一個圖片學生多半能描述因應之道（如改變目的地或轉換心情）。考生只要能依題意合理說明每個圖片的情境及後續發展，若內容組織及文字使用沒有太多錯誤，應能拿到不錯的分數。

extraction.method: 題本文字以 Word 版 paper-2.docx 為主（直接走訪 document.xml 的 w:r，含 w:hyperlink 內的文字；底線數字 run 轉成 [[題號]]），再以程式將全部 260 段文字（說明、選文各段、題幹、選項、選項庫）與 pdftotext -layout（paper-1.pdf）的詞序列逐段比對，全部一致；Read 看 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像確認版面、粗體／斜體與底線，英文作文四格漫畫另以 pdftoppm -r 300 放大裁切判讀；答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext -layout）；評分原則取自 scoring.pdf（pdftotext 與 -layout，並以頁面影像核對段落順序）逐字摘錄；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英文工作表：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D）、stats-2.xls（英文工作表：選項分析 T／H／L 列、未答）、stats-3.xls（英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表），並以程式交叉核對（選項分析標 * 的選項＝官方答案；其 T／H／L 比例＝P／Ph／Pl；D＝Ph−Pl；非選擇題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數）。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 期別「94–110」一致——詞彙題 1–15（15分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，題組標示16–20、21–25、26–30，15分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，10分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，每題2分，32分）、中譯英 2題×4分、英文作文 20分（文長至少120個單詞）；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分；封面「考試時間：100 分鐘」「單選題共 56 題」「非選擇題共二大題」。無差異。
validator warning「題號重複 [1, 2]」為預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）；no 必須是整數，故沿用題本編號，並以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「作文」區分，label 無重複。

中譯英：評分原則沒有公布完整參考譯文，只指出常見錯誤（第一句「整個」應譯出 entire 或 whole、「覆蓋著」應用被動語態 is covered；第二句「征服」應用動名詞 conquering、「挑戰」challenges 應拼對且用複數），故 answer 與 accepted_answers 皆為 null。評分原則中與中譯英相關的段落同時談到兩句，無法逐句切開而不破壞原文，故兩題的 scoring_notes 都放「評分標準與歷年相同…每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。」加上整段中譯英說明（逐字）。

英文作文：評分原則沒有官方範文，answer 為 null；題目沒有規定段數，tags 不填 paragraphs。scoring_notes 由評分原則三處逐字摘錄組成（「英文作文」評分標準句、第一段中「第二大題是「英文作文」，今年為看圖寫作…文長至少 120 個單詞。」、最後一段看圖寫作說明），以換行分隔。本年評分項目寫作「詞彙拼字」（四項：內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字），與 spec 所記 106 年起改為四項一致。
英文作文四格漫畫（s6g1 figures）：依 300dpi 頁面影像判讀描述。圖3 的建築物外觀（拱形窗、欄杆）無法確定是哪一類景點；評分原則說明考生將第三圖寫成遊樂園、博物館、動物園、演唱會、遊行示威人潮或出國過海關等場景皆可，故描述中只寫「大型建築（景點）前擠滿人潮」，不指定場所。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 只有「第一題（中譯英，滿分8分，兩小題合計）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，無法拆到中譯英各小題，因此放在 sections[s5].stats 與 sections[s6].stats 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義此欄位，沿用 gsat-107/109 的做法）；rate 為原表百分比÷100，分母是報名人數 128,760（含缺考 2,058；到考 126,702），已核對各分數段人數加總＝到考人數。原表分數區間「9.00- 9.99」等的空白已去除；本年作文最高分段原表寫作「20.00-20.99」（與他年「20.00-20.00」寫法不同），照原表保留。小題層級 stats 為 null。

選擇題統計：除 schema 欄位外，另存 option_rates_high／option_rates_low（stats-2.xls 選項分析的高分組 H、低分組 L 列）與 omit_rate（全體未答比例，T 列；第56題 T 列未答 1%）；stats-1.xls 的五組通過率 Pa–Pe 與 D1–D4 未收錄。已程式核對全部 56 題：選項分析中標 * 的選項＝官方答案，且其 T／H／L 比例＝P／Ph／Pl，D＝Ph−Pl，題號對齊無誤。各題 option_rates（加未答）因四捨五入加總為 0.99–1.01。

低答對率／低鑑別度題目已複核非對齊錯誤（皆為大考中心原始數據）：第22題 P=0.21、D=0.09（43% 選 A get done）；第16題 P=0.40、D=0.16（28% 選 D see through）；第28題 P=0.36、D=0.17；第11題 P=0.25（四個選項各約 24–27%）；第21題 P=0.24；第20題 P=0.28（42% 選 B among）；第27題 P=0.28（44% 選 B link）；第43題 P=0.29（41% 選 A Creative measurement）。

格式：題本中第41–44題選文與第43題的 venture、第49–52題選文與第52題的 Others、第53–56題選文與第54題的 a lasting British institution 為粗體；第46、55題的 NOT 為粗體；第21–25題選文的 The Shoe That Grows 與第49–52題選文的 Harper’s Weekly 為斜體；「第16至20題為題組」等題組標示有底線。第43、52、54題被問的粗體字在選文對應位置已加 <b>（不是底線，所以不用 <u>）並填 refers_to；題幹的粗體、NOT 與斜體依規定不保留格式。

文字來源：Word 版中 swollen、Dognition、nine categories、Dognition’s Facebook page、Catherine of Braganza 等字包在超連結（w:hyperlink）內，只讀 run 會漏字，已改為走訪 XML 取得並與 PDF 核對無誤。PDF 選項庫 I 印作「( I ) symbols」（括號內有空白），代號統一為 I。第42題 (D)「the score of a Dognition’s test」照題本原文保留。第26題空格後的逗號依題本緊接空格（「[[26]], many people…」）。
評分原則 PDF 無 CJK 相容表意字（NFC 正規化前後相同）；pdftotext 非 layout 模式會把「。使用的字都在詞彙表四級內」排到「第二句則為…」之前，已依頁面影像與 -layout 輸出還原正確順序。

本檔新增的非 schema 欄位：section.part_title／part_instructions（第壹、貳部分標題與第貳部分共同說明，放在該部分的第一個大題 s1、s5）、section.stats（非選擇題分數分布）、group.group_label（「第16至20題為題組」等題本原文）、figure.label、sources.paper_word、question.stats.option_rates_high／option_rates_low／omit_rate。
